key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, electrostatic storage, and low-power ferroelectric computing should be co-designed so edge AI nodes can operate reliably without depending on centralized data centers.
engineering_relevance: The paper frames (anti)ferroelectric materials as a practical route to combine local energy harvesting, buffering, and in-memory computation for sustainable distributed intelligence.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaics against edge-device energy needs
Survey emerging materials for energy storage and neuromorphic/in-memory computing
Identify where (anti)ferroelectrics can reduce power and close system-level gaps
evidence_signal: This is a perspective paper, so the evidence is a requirements analysis and materials comparison rather than a new experimental benchmark dataset.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is that reliable edge AI will still depend on matching device energy supply, storage, and compute performance under real indoor conditions.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
